key_insight: Intra-patient 3D multimodal deformable registration remains unsolved, with methods that improve overlap often failing to improve global multimodal structural alignment.
engineering_relevance: For clinical imaging pipelines, this means registration models must be validated with multiple complementary metrics, not just Dice or Hausdorff distance, to avoid misleading performance gains.
method: Benchmarked classical optimization-based, deep learning, and foundation-model registration methods.
Tested across three datasets spanning synthetic deformation recovery and real clinical cases.
Evaluated with DSC, HD95, and MIND-SSC to capture overlap, boundary error, and modality-independent similarity.
evidence_signal: Across three datasets, learning-based methods performed best on large synthetic benchmarks, but gains were limited in real pelvic registration and geometric metrics often disagreed with MIND-SSC.
watch_item: Anatomy-guided methods can inflate overlap scores inside segmented regions while degrading alignment outside them, so deployment should check for global deformation quality.
paper_title: Benchmarking Intra-Patient 3D Deformable Multimodal Image Registration
